answer_1.quote: We present a simple yet novel testbed with: (i) an LLM personified as a lobbyist, proposing amendments in legislative bills with explicitly declared altruistic agenda but with deceptively hidden benefits to a benefactor company...

answer_2.quote: We evaluate the two conflicting goals of the lobbyist as follows: (a) Identification Rate: The critic's success, and thus the lobbyist's deception failure, is measured by the critic's identification rate of the hidden benefactor c * . (b) Benefit Capture Rate: The average of the lobbyist's evaluation score (S eval ) over all simulations, measuring the overall benefits captured in amendments.

answer_3.quote: We implement this scoring by performing pairwise comparisons and reducing them to a single score per company... We query the critic which of a pair (c 1 , c 2 ) of companies benefit more from a bill, given its details and those of companies c 1 , c 2 .

answer_4.quote: We verify three important aspects for the quality of generations through human evaluations: 1. Benefit captured in the generated amendments (Ques. 1 and 2 in Table ). 2. Verify the substantialness of the benefits planned by the lobbyist. (Ques. 3) 3. Verify that the quality of re-planning reasoning captures the intended benefits to the benefactor correctly. (Ques. 4)
answer_4.guideline: 1. Benefit captured in the generated amendments. 2. Verify the substantialness of the benefits planned by the lobbyist. 3. Verify that the quality of re-planning reasoning captures the intended benefits to the benefactor correctly.
